title: Total of the Most Frequent Values
statement:
You get an array of positive integers nums. The frequency of a value is how many times it appears. Find the highest frequency, then return how many elements of the array have a value with that frequency.

In other words: add up the frequencies of every value that is tied for most frequent.

examples.why: 4 and 7 both appear twice, the most of any value. Together they account for 4 elements.
Every value appears once, so all three are tied for most frequent.
Only 5 has the top frequency 3. The answer counts its elements (3), not the number of top values (1).

hints: First you need the frequency of every value. Which structure gives that in one pass?
Once you have the counts, find the largest one, then add up every count equal to it.
You can do it in the same pass: keep the best frequency so far and the running total, and reset the total whenever a count beats the best.

explain.intuition:
Count every value with a hash map, like tallying votes. The top frequency is the largest tally. Every value tied at the top contributes all of its copies, so the answer is top × (number of values at top).

The one-pass version keeps best and total while counting. When a value's count rises above best, it is the new sole leader, so total becomes that count. When it ties best, add best to the total.
steps: Count each value in a map.
Add up every count equal to top and return the sum.
pitfalls: Returning the number of values tied at the top instead of the number of elements. [4, 4, 7, 7, 2] is 4, not 2.
In the one-pass version, forgetting to reset the total when a new maximum appears.

solutions.title: Count, then sum the top counts
solutions.idea: Tally every value, find the largest tally, and add up every tally that equals it.

solutions.title: One pass
solutions.idea: Update the leader and the running total as each count grows.

followups: The values arrive as a stream and you must answer after each one. Does the one-pass version already do that?
Return the values tied for most frequent, sorted.
